AMBIENT WATCH LOOP triggers - edit to opt in, no code changes needed.

Each trigger has:
  id        - unique name (appears in var/logs/tasks.jsonl as watch:<id>)
  goal      - the goal string, planned through L4 (one LLM call per distinct
              goal per daemon run, then cached) OR
  plan      - an inline deterministic plan dict (no LLM; must be fully
              resolved - no $facts refs)
  schedule  - {"type": "time", "at": "HH:MM", "days": ["mon"...]} fires once
              per day after the time; {"type": "file", "directory": ...,"name":
              <substring>, "recursive": bool} fires once per new matching file
  enabled   - false means the trigger is inert; set true to activate
  notify    - send a desktop notification when the trigger finishes (default true)
  allow     - OPTIONAL primitive allowlist: a list of exact names or 'mod.*' patterns.
              If present, any plan step whose primitive is NOT on the list is REFUSED
              before execution (recorded as REFUSED, never executed) - for unattended
              triggers whose LLM plan must be constrained (L2 verify checks are
              read-only and always permitted).

CURRENTLY ENABLED (2026-08-14):
- morning-gmail-summary (09:00 weekdays) - the live LLM-planned trigger. Its goal
  references $facts.gmail_sender (edit config/planner_facts.json, never the trigger).
  Allowlist TIGHTENED to the three read-only primitives (gmail.list_unread /
  gmail.get_message / gmail.summarize) so the LLM plan can never reach the
  gate-registered send primitive (gmail.send_document). An empty mailbox for that
  sender is an honest FAIL, never an error.
- weekly-cross-project-digest (Sun 10:00, Phase C v2.2) - a DETERMINISTIC plan (no
  L4 LLM call) gathering git.log from Friday + vivaha + Aether, each repo's most
  recently modified status/planning doc (files.find_recent_doc), reads those docs,
  then dev.digest - the ONE live full-tier LLM call (~$0.17/run), verified by
  digestcheck.verify_attribution (no repo may be credited with a mechanism not in
  its own gathered content) and delivered via notify.notify_send. Repo paths are
  hardcoded (deterministic plans must be fully resolved); edit if repos move.
  Agent-Reach is deliberately excluded (third-party, not owned); Psyche Space and
  ChangelogAI excluded pending a separate decision. Human verdicts are logged in
  gates/DIGEST_TRACKING.md.
- sunday-digest-reminder (Sun 10:05) - one-step deterministic notify-only plan
  (allow [notify.notify_send], notify:false so it never double-pings) nudging the
  weekly verdict into gates/DIGEST_TRACKING.md.

RETIRED ambient-gap-probe-* triggers (all DISABLED - the gap-loop lifecycle):
- ambient-gap-probe-email-send (2026-08-11): gmail.send_document hand-built, gated,
  human-signed, registered - the loop's first side-effecting primitive.
- ambient-gap-probe-file-write (2026-08-13): files.write_text approved + registered
  through the full loop (self-checked LLM draft, automated gate with write-family
  build-verify, human review, register); remaining gaps are consumed as SOLVED.
- ambient-gap-probe-calendar (2026-08-13): calendar.list_upcoming registered through
  the loop's second complete cycle (LLM-drafted with ZERO hand-correction, gate with
  build-verify honestly NOT APPLICABLE for the calendar class, human-signed). Note:
  it needs calendar OAuth creds (pass friday/calendar or GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TOKEN) to
  return real events; without them it returns [] and verification fails honestly.

ACTIVE (2026-08-14):
- ambient-gap-probe-clipboard (daily 11:00) - the loop's new ambient volume source
  after all three originals retired. Its single step is clipboard.read_text, a
  genuinely UNBUILT primitive (no clipboard module exists in friday/l1) that is NOT
  deliberately deferred by the plan (unlike vision, gated off, and window.shutdown,
  mechanically blocked) - so its daily refusal is a real gap, not noise. Allowlist
  refuses before any execution (zero side effects); REFUSED is terminal-for-the-day;
  exactly one capability-gap record per day for triage to LLM-draft. Retire it once
  clipboard.read_text is approved and registered (lifecycle precedent: the three
  above).

Lifecycle rule: once a probe's primitive is approved and registered, RETIRE the probe
- its daily refusal of a now-solved primitive is noise. The loop's ambient volume now
comes from the active probe above plus real refusals and the goal-proposals stage;
see the README.

Safety is inherited from the core: the executor refuses blocked primitives, window
close never touches protected classes, dev.run_shell needs FRIDAY_ALLOW_DANGEROUS=1,
and triggers run strictly one at a time.

Run once (for cron / testing):  ./.venv/bin/python -m friday.watcher --once
Run as a daemon:               ./.venv/bin/python -m friday.watcher --poll 30
